signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + BoJ Intervention Threshold
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 160.1, breaching the critical 160.00 psychological level following TIER-1 headlines of an Iranian IRGC blockade in the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the geopolitical escalation, JPY is not attracting safe-haven flows as the VIX remains at 14.4, a risk-on print below the safe-haven threshold; instead, the pair is driven by the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage and a hawkish Fed Chair Warsh headline. Speculative positioning remains heavily short JPY with LF net at -73,641 (pctl 12), while the options market signals acute fear of a reversal with a strong 25d RR put skew of -1.81. The break above 160.00 directly triggers BoJ intervention risk, especially as the pair now trades above its SMA20/200 cluster but remains below the SMA50 at 160.86. Trade bias: Neutral/Short USD/JPY; intervention risk outweighs carry persistence at these levels. Catalyst: BoJ board member Tamura speech at Jackson Hole. Risk: BoJ remains on the sidelines, allowing carry-chasing to extend the rally toward 162.00.

signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Commodity Bid
signals.text: AUD/CHF has emerged as the dominant G10 trend this week, with AUD outperforming peers by +1.308% while CHF lags at -0.809%, creating a 2.117% spread. This bilateral divergence is supported by a significant 435bp carry premium in favor of the AUD (RBA 4.35% vs SNB 0.0%) and an accommodative real rate in CHF of -1.24%. While AUD positioning is becoming crowded with LF net long at +49,749 (pctl 94, z +1.78), the retail market is at a 94% short extreme in AUD/CHF, providing a contrarian tailwind for further upside. The pair remains technically bid, supported by the AUD/USD position above its SMA20/50/200 cluster. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/CHF; carry advantage and retail short-squeeze support the trend. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep for regional cross-flows. Risk: VIX spikes above 25, triggering a rapid unwind of the high-carry AUD/CHF long.

signals.title: GBP/USD — BoE Neutrality vs High Vol Risk Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3534, testing its SMA20 support at 1.3537 as Governor Bailey signals muted inflation effects ahead of the September meeting. While the Fed-BoE nominal carry is neutral at 0bp, the options market is pricing in significant protection with a 6.0-point Vol Risk Premium (IV 11.0% vs HV30 5.0%). Speculative positioning in GBP is increasingly crowded, with LF net long at +46,070 (pctl 92, z +1.22), leaving the pair vulnerable to a long-unwind if BoE hold pricing (currently 100%) shifts toward a dovish bias. The UK 10Y yield at 5.07% maintains a +39bp spread over US Treasuries, but disappointing ESI data (-9.3) suggests macro fundamentals are beginning to lag the price action. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; crowded positioning and high VRP suggest limited upside. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep. Risk: Fed Chair Warsh commentary triggers a broad USD rally that forces a break of the 1.3418/1.3437 SMA50/200 support cluster.

signals.title: USD/CAD — BoC Press Conference + ESI Divergence
signals.text: USD/CAD sits at 1.3905, supported by a 150bp Fed-BoC carry advantage and strong US data repricing following hawkish Fed commentary. This move contrasts with CAD's positive Economic Surprise Index (index +20.8), where sustained data beats have failed to support the currency against the USD's policy dominance. Speculative positioning remains extremely short CAD with LF net at -89,836 (pctl 3, z -2.07), a level historically associated with exhaustion and reversal risk. The pair is currently trading below its SMA20 (1.3910) and SMA50 (1.4045), suggesting the immediate trend is consolidating despite the broader carry bid. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD; technical resistance and extreme CAD spec shorts favor a tactical retracement. Catalyst: BoC Governor Macklem press conference 9 Sep. Risk: Oil prices collapse further on Strait of Hormuz news, overriding the spec short-squeeze potential.
